message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00, which filled at $223.00 — about $9,812, inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily cap, with no cash transferred out and only the permitted AAPL/MSFT universe used. The limit was set 0.13% above the last quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so it was close to market rather than a stretched price. The filing supports a constructive view: total net sales of $391.0 billion (+2% y/y), with Services up 13% to $96.2 billion and Services gross margin of 73.9% lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion and operating cash flow was strong at $118.3 billion. Reported net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly y/y, but that decline was driven by a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not by operating deterioration. Balanced against that, iPhone sales were flat at $201.2 billion, Greater China fell 8%, and Wearables declined 7%, and the stock at ~$223 trades at roughly 37x trailing EPS, so I sized the position modestly (about 20% of cash) rather than committing the full daily allowance. (Note: the statements-of-operations line in the filing text showed a garbled "94,930" for total net sales; I used the $391,035 million figure confirmed by both the segment and product-category tables.)
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00, $9,812. Summarize.

Note the filing text had a garbled "Total net sales 94,930" typo in the statements of operations — the correct figure per segment/category tables is $391,035M. I used 391,035.
